title: This Animal Can't Sweat or Pant, So It Blows Snot Bubbles to Cool Down
subject: short-beaked echidna

scenes.text: This animal can't sweat, can't pant, and can't lick itself. So how does it survive a heatwave?
It's the short-beaked echidna. In Western Australia, the ground around it can hit 47 degrees Celsius.
Old lab studies said echidnas shouldn't survive above 35 degrees. Wild ones were sheltering in logs at 40.
Curtin University scientists checked 124 wild echidnas with thermal cameras. The coolest part of each was the tip of the beak.
The trick: the echidna blows a bubble of wet mucus from its nose. When it bursts, the film evaporates and cools the blood in the beak.
Snot bubbles. It's the air conditioning of one of the world's strangest mammals.

description:
Echidnas can't sweat, pant or lick themselves, yet they survive outback heat.
Scientists found they blow snot bubbles that evaporate and cool the blood in their beak.
Would you trade your sweat for a snot bubble? Tell us below.
